questions.scenario: DC Lewis is planning her NIE revision. She asks how many questions she must answer correctly to pass, given that only some of the 80 questions are scored.
explanations: Correct: the pass mark is 55.7 %, which is 39 of the 70 scored questions.
Wrong: only 70 questions are scored, not all 80.
Wrong: 40/70 would be 57.1 %; the pass mark is 39/70 (55.7 %).
Wrong: the exam has 80 questions, not 100.

questions.scenario: A trainee finds a great explanation of a point of law in an online article that disagrees with the current Blackstone's Manual. Which source will the NIE question follow?
options: The online article if it is more recent
Blackstone's Police Investigators' Manual for the exam year
Whichever source the trainee's tutor prefers
explanations: Wrong: questions are not based on outside sources, however recent.
Correct: NIE questions come only from the Blackstone's Manual for the exam year.
Wrong: the exam does not depend on a tutor's preference.
Wrong: useful for learning, but exam questions come only from the Manual.

questions.scenario: During the NIE, a candidate is stuck on question 12 after 4 minutes. With 80 questions in 120 minutes, what is the best strategy?
options: Keep working on it until it is solved
Choose the best answer, flag it and move on
explanations: Wrong: the average is 90 seconds per question; spending 4+ minutes costs easier marks later.
Wrong: there is no benefit in leaving early.
Correct: answer, flag it for review and keep moving; come back if time allows.
Wrong: always give an answer — a blank scores nothing.

questions.scenario: A candidate decides not to bother with 10 'hard-looking' questions, believing they are the unscored ones. Is this a good idea?
options: Yes, the hardest questions are always the unscored ones
No: you cannot know which 10 questions are unscored
Yes, as long as the other 70 are correct
No, because all 80 questions are scored
explanations: Wrong: nothing tells you which questions are unscored.
Correct: treat every question as if it counts.
Wrong: you cannot identify the unscored ones, so you risk losing real marks.
Wrong: only 70 are scored — but you still can't tell which.

questions.scenario: Clara wants to use an AI chatbot on her phone to check an answer during the NIE. What is the position?
options: Allowed for questions on Part 4 only
explanations: Wrong: no AI use is permitted.
Wrong: AI use during the exam is prohibited.
Correct: using AI during the NIE is prohibited.
Wrong: the ban applies to the whole exam.
